subject: Science
chapter: Topic-based: use with whichever Class 9 book your students follow
title: Quick Revision: Gravitation

table: Amount of matter; same everywhere; kg
Force of gravity on a body, W = mg; newton (N)
Thrust is force acting perpendicular to a surface; pressure = thrust ÷ area, in pascal (Pa)
The upward force a fluid exerts on an object in it

bullets: If the distance between two bodies is doubled, the force becomes **one-fourth**.
All objects fall with the same acceleration g in the absence of air resistance (free fall).
Weight on the Moon is about **one-sixth** of the weight on Earth; mass does not change.
g is slightly greater at the poles than at the equator, because the Earth's radius is smaller at the poles.
Sharp knives cut easily and camels have broad feet: same force, smaller or larger area changes the pressure.
**Archimedes' principle:** a body fully or partly immersed in a fluid feels an upward force equal to the weight of the fluid it displaces. An object floats if its density is less than the liquid's.

box: Equations of motion for free fall: replace a with g (and use −g for a body thrown up).
Relative density = density of the substance ÷ density of water (no unit)
